passages.title: Sara's Busy Day
passages.body:
Sara is sixteen years old and she lives in Isfahan with her parents and her little brother, Amir. On school days, she gets up at six thirty. She has breakfast with her family, usually bread, cheese and tea. Then she walks to school with her best friend, Neda. The walk takes about fifteen minutes.

School starts at seven forty-five and finishes at one thirty. Sara's favourite subject is English, but she finds maths difficult. After school, she has lunch at home and rests for an hour. In the afternoon, she does her homework and practises English for twenty minutes on her phone.

On Tuesdays and Thursdays, Sara goes to a swimming class. She is not a fast swimmer, but she enjoys it a lot. In the evening, she helps Amir with his reading. She usually goes to bed at ten thirty.

passages.title: The Friday Market
passages.body:
Every Friday morning, there is a big market in the main square of our town. It opens at seven and closes at noon. Farmers from the villages near the town come to sell fresh fruit, vegetables, eggs and honey. You can also find cheap clothes, old books and handmade bags.

My grandmother loves this market. She says the fruit is fresher and cheaper than in the supermarket. She always buys tomatoes, cucumbers and a big bag of oranges. I go with her because I like the old book stall. Last week I bought two English storybooks for a very good price.

The market is very crowded after nine o'clock, so we usually go early. It is also a good place to meet neighbours and friends. For many people in our town, Friday is not complete without a visit to the market.

passages.title: A Holiday in Gilan
passages.body:
Dear Mina,

I hope you are well. I am writing to you from Gilan! My family and I arrived in Rasht three days ago. The weather here is very different from Tehran. It rains a lot, and everything is green.

On our first day, we visited the old bazaar in Rasht. We tried a lot of local food. My favourite was a dish with eggplant and garlic. Yesterday we drove to Masuleh, a beautiful village in the mountains. The houses there are built on top of each other, so the roof of one house is the yard of another house! We walked for hours and took many photos.

Tomorrow we are going to the sea. I hope it doesn't rain. We are going back home on Sunday. I will show you all my photos when I see you.

Love,
Parisa

passages.title: The New Library
passages.body:
Last month, a new public library opened in our neighbourhood. It is a large, bright building with big windows and a small garden. The library is open from nine in the morning to eight in the evening, every day except Friday.

There are more than twenty thousand books on three floors. The ground floor has books for children and a quiet corner where parents can read to their kids. The first floor has novels, history books and magazines. On the second floor, there are computers and study rooms for students.

Membership is free, but you need an ID card to join. Members can borrow up to four books for two weeks. If you return a book late, you pay a small fine. Every Wednesday evening, the library has an English conversation club. Anyone can join, and it is free for members.
